children: It's not entirely clear if FX intervention drove the yen's sharp strengthening overnight, but BOJ current-account data suggest that wasn't the case, says MUFG's Michael Wan. A clearer driver was a speech from BOJ hawk Takata this week that markets took as signaling that the door to an outsized rate hike is open. That led the JPY OIS market to start to price in some chance--albeit small--of a more than 25bp hike in September, a view the BOJ doesn't seem to share, says Wan. Remarks from Fed governor Waller overnight saying he was leaning toward a rate hold if inflation continues to slow contributed too. That tracks with MUFG's view that pricing for Fed hikes are excessive and that the dollar should weaken over time. The dollar is little changed at 155.89 yen. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)
